digest.component_or_area: completion-verifier epic-close bug screen and gate
propositions: The epic-close bug screen degrades per-candidate LLM provider failures (including systematic outages like Bedrock 400s) to verdict C ('unrelated'), silently blinding the caused_by bug floor instead of failing the close.

When all 32 screen candidates fail due to a Bedrock ValidationException (max_tokens exceeding model ceiling), the verifier returns PASS with no aggregate signal, no error exit, and no indication that the screen was blind.
max_tokens request ceiling set for a 128K model is never re-clamped when a later screen call resolves to a 64K model, causing Bedrock to reject with 400 on every haiku attempt.

LLMUnavailableError (including subclass LLMConfigError) must propagate from the completion-verifier's epic-close bug screen instead of degrading to C, failing the close consistently with the absent-provider path.
The completion-verifier run must fail closed (nonzero exit, in_progress ticket, error naming provider failure) on any LLMUnavailableError, with --force-close as the documented escape hatch.
Non-systemic per-candidate failures (malformed output, store errors) must continue to degrade to C per documented behavior, so only provider-class errors trigger fail-closed behavior.
